info.title: tesseract-rs OCR
info.description: Pure-Rust, byte-parity Tesseract OCR (English + German models) exposed as a Power Platform custom connector. Recognize a document image into structured tesseract-rs/doc.v1 JSON (text/table/figure/header/footer regions, reconstructed table cell grids, per-word confidence, typed field harvest), or export a searchable or structured PDF. Zero C libraries at runtime. See https://github.com/AdaWorldAPI/tesseract-rs.

api_key.name: x-api-key
api_key.description: Optional shared-secret gate. Only enforced when the deployment sets the TESSERACT_API_KEY environment variable; otherwise every request is accepted (the server's default, open demo mode). See integrations/power-platform/README.md.

post.description: Decodes an image (PNG/JPEG/WebP/TIFF/GIF/BMP/PNM) and returns the structured tesseract-rs/doc.v1 document: text/table/figure/header/footer regions, reconstructed table cell grids, per-word confidence, and a typed field harvest (amounts, IBANs, GUIDs). Primary input is the raw image bytes (application/octet-stream) - this matches Microsoft Graph's 'Get file content' output byte-for-byte, so a SharePoint/OneDrive/Outlook-attachment flow can pass the file content straight through with no conversion step. lang selects the recognition model: eng (default) or deu; an unrecognized value falls back to eng rather than erroring. For a binary body, pass lang via the ?lang= query parameter (there is no body field to carry it); for a JSON body, send {"content_base64": "<base64>", "lang": "eng"} instead (the JSON field wins if both are somehow present). rectify optionally runs page rectification (auto-corrects rotational skew and first-order keystone/trapezoid distortion from a photographed page) before recognition; it is always a safe no-op on an already-straight page.

parameters.name: lang
parameters.description: Recognition model for a binary (application/octet-stream) body. Ignored when the body is application/json - use the JSON form's own lang field there instead.

parameters.name: rectify
parameters.description: Runs page rectification (auto-corrects rotational skew and first-order keystone/trapezoid distortion from a photographed page) before recognition. For a JSON body, this combines with the body's own rectify field - true from either source enables it (unlike lang, there is no 'which one wins', since a plain flag has no competing values to choose between). Always a safe no-op on an already-straight page - never fails a request that would otherwise succeed.

parameters.name: body
parameters.description: Raw image bytes (application/octet-stream), e.g. the binary output of a 'Get file content' action. When Content-Type is application/json instead, send {"content_base64": "...", "lang": "eng", "rectify": false} (see the RecognizeJsonBody definition).

200.description: The recognized document as tesseract-rs/doc.v1 JSON.

400.description: The image could not be decoded, was too large/small, or the JSON body was malformed.

401.description: Missing or invalid x-api-key header (only enforced when TESSERACT_API_KEY is configured server-side).

503.description: The server is shutting down and is not accepting new recognition work.

post.description: Recognizes the input image and renders a PDF. Default: the original scan raster with an invisible, selectable text layer (mode=searchable). Pass ?mode=structured for the doc.v1-driven layout reconstruction instead - equivalent to calling the dedicated StructuredPdf action below. Same input shapes as RecognizeDocument (binary, or {content_base64, lang, rectify} JSON); lang selects eng (default) or deu the same way, and rectify optionally runs page rectification before recognition (see RecognizeDocument's rectify parameter).

parameters.name: mode
parameters.description: PDF reconstruction mode. searchable (default): original raster + invisible text layer. structured: doc.v1 layout reconstruction (same as the StructuredPdf action).

post.description: A query-param-free-for-mode alias for POST /api/v1/pdf?mode=structured, exposed as its own action so it is directly selectable in the Power Automate action picker. Renders the doc.v1 layout reconstruction ('B'): regions, tables, and figures laid out from the recognized structure rather than the original scan raster. Same input shapes as RecognizeDocument; ?lang= is still accepted (there is no mode to select here, but the language switch is orthogonal), and so is ?rectify= (see RecognizeDocument's rectify parameter).

get.description: Cheap liveness probe: no request body, no recognition work, no auth. Reports which recognition models this deployment actually loaded at startup (eng is always present; deu only when the deployment's model directory has the deu.lstm* components). Use this as the connector's Test-operation target, or poll it from an external monitor.

200.description: The server is up; models lists the loaded language codes.

content_base64.description: Base64-encoded image bytes (standard or URL-safe alphabet, padded or not).

lang.description: Selects the recognition model: eng (default) or deu. An unrecognized value falls back to eng rather than erroring. deu is only available when the deployment's model directory has the deu.lstm* components; otherwise a deu request also falls back to eng.

rectify.description: Runs page rectification (auto-corrects rotational skew and first-order keystone/trapezoid distortion from a photographed page) before recognition. Combines with the rectify query parameter via OR - true from either source enables it. Always a safe no-op on an already-straight page - never fails a request that would otherwise succeed.

BBox.description: [left, top, right, bottom] in image pixels, top-down origin.

numeric_norm.description: Present only when numeric hardening changed the recognized text (e.g. OCR'd 'O' corrected to '0').

type.description: text | table | figure | header | footer | paragraph. Additive: ignore unrecognized values.

cells.description: Table regions only: the reconstructed cell grid.

value_cents.description: Present when the field is a hardened monetary amount.

mean_conf.description: Mean word confidence 0-100, or null when the page has no words.

low_confidence.description: true suggests handwriting, low resolution, or non-printed input.

plain_text.description: The whole page as one string (every recognized word, joined the same way the plain-text renderer does: leading_space-aware, lines separated by \n). Ergonomics for low-code flows that just want the text, not the region/line/word tree - e.g. piping straight into "Send an email" or "Post a message". Always present, even on an empty page (""), never null.

fields_map.description: The same values as fields, reshaped key -> value. Finding one field in the fields array needs a Filter-Array + First() expression in the Power Automate designer; fields_map['iban'] is a single dynamic-content lookup. Always present, even with no harvested fields ({}), never null. Duplicate keys keep the last value.

DocV1.description: tesseract-rs/doc.v1 - the canonical structured OCR document.

models.description: Recognition models this deployment loaded at startup ("eng", optionally "deu").
